رَحُومٌ (Lh, S, K) and ↓ رَحْمَآءُ , (K,) applied to a she-camel, (Lh, S, TA,) and to a ewe or she-goat, and to a woman, (TA,) [and app. to any animal having a womb, (see رَحُمَتْ)] Having a complaint of her womb (Lh, S, M, K) after bringing forth, (Lh, S, K,) and dying in consequence thereof; (K;) and ↓ رَحِمَةٌ , applied to a she-camel, signifies the same: the pl. of رَحُومٌ is رُحُمٌ, with two dammehs. (TA.) ―
-b2- For the first, see also الرَّحْمٰنُ, near the end of the paragraph.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
